picks.why: XLE's largest holding (22%) has finally joined the breakout, up 4.09% to $165.99 with RSI only 51 and 3% below its 52-week high, so it has the most room of the leaders while WTI holds $100 with Hormuz constrained, Bab el-Mandeb threatened and no OPEC+ meeting until Oct 4.

The largest pure oil producer on the sheet closed at a fresh 52-week high ($137.35), yet producer stocks still lag $100 crude, so it can re-rate on a one-and-done hike or a worse supply shock, with the average analyst target about 6% above the price.

The sector's strongest trend (+66% in 12 weeks, fresh 52-week-high close) is backed by record diesel refining margins above $100 a barrel and ~97% utilization, which the Houthi push on Bab el-Mandeb can only tighten; I take it despite an overbought RSI of 80.

It is the high-beta way to play faster AI demand: its Helios rack system began shipping and management put its 2030 market at $2T, driving an 8.07% rally on that news while the chip ETF (SMH) was flat, and it would lead XLK through $188.74 if Wednesday's hike is framed as insurance.

It is the biggest lever on the healthcare bounce: at about 12% of XLV it sits at an RSI of 2.5, about 5% above its 200-day ($1,062), after selling driven by higher rates and a knock-on from a rival's failed heart-drug trial rather than any damage to its obesity-drug sales, so a one-and-done Fed should lift it first.

summary: Energy is my only confirmed breakout and the book's hedge if the dot plot reads hawkish, so it takes three slots: XOM, COP and VLO; AMD and LLY pay if Wednesday's ~90%-priced hike reads as insurance. I leave Communication Services out (META at RSI 84 would be a chase), and BTC and GLD sit out a week with a Fed hike Wednesday and a BOJ hike Friday.
